svg.title: MVPN profiles and the bandwidth arithmetic of default MDT versus data MDT
svg.desc: Left: five MVPN profiles compared. Rosen GRE with PIM between PEs, medium complexity and good compatibility. Rosen mLDP profile 1 using a point-to-multipoint LSP as the MDT, the modern mainstream. Rosen RSVP-TE P2MP profile 2, used when traffic engineering is required. Partitioned MDT profile 3, for very large scale with reduced PE full mesh. BGP auto-discovery profile 14 with selective trees, used by modern carriers. Right: the arithmetic that decides whether data MDT is optional. With 100 PEs and one 50 Mbps group, a default MDT only design replicates to 99 PEs, which is 4.95 Gbps of mostly useless traffic; a data MDT limited to the 4 PEs that really have receivers carries 200 Mbps. Bottom: the three concepts to keep apart - default MDT or I-PMSI carries everything including low bitrate, data MDT or S-PMSI carries only high bitrate groups to interested PEs, and the PE runs PIM or IGMP proxy toward the CE so the CE never needs to know about MPLS.
svg.text: MVPN: five profiles, and one arithmetic that decides whether they work
An MPLS L3VPN carries no multicast until you deploy one of these. The profile is the easy choice; the MDT sizing is the one that hurts.
the oldest option, and the one that still appears in brownfield networks
labels instead of tunnel headers: no GRE overhead, no PIM in the core
only when multicast needs traffic engineering or bandwidth reservation
breaks the every-PE-in-every-MDT problem when the PE count is in the hundreds
selective trees chosen by the PE, not by a static profile definition
95 of those PEs have no receivers at all
the tree follows the receivers, not the PE count
this is a bandwidth bill, not a configuration detail
every PE joins, every group crosses,
only the PEs with receivers join,
which is why it must be enabled -
it is a requirement, not a tuning knob
PIM or IGMP proxy toward the CE,
MDT toward the other PEs. The RP
sits on the CE (autonomy) or the PE (transparency)
Acceptance test that finds this early: send one 50 Mbps group between two VRFs whose receivers are in one site only, then look at the egress counters of a PE that has no receiver.
If that PE shows the full stream, data MDT is not working - and nobody will notice until the first all-hands webcast fills the backbone.
